minutes.headline: Select Board reorganized: new chair, vice chair and clerk elected, two newly-elected members seated
minutes.summary: This was the Select Board's annual reorganization meeting following the town election: the board elected a chair, vice chair and clerk, seated two new members, and reassigned liaison duties to boards and committees. Substantive items included a public hearing approving a one-day liquor license for a church anniversary event, a letter of support for a state bill (S400) to reform the Chapter 70 school funding formula, delegating unregistered-vehicle enforcement to the building commissioner, and extended discussion (not finalized) of a townwide sick leave bank policy and what to do with a tax-title property at 56 Cara Sell.

public_comment.topic: Board members (not the public) welcomed the two newly elected select board members and congratulated all election candidates; no public speakers came forward.
Introduced the special event license application for the parish's 75th ('Diamond Jubilee') anniversary celebration on June 22.
Described the Diamond Jubilee event plans, free-will-donation ticketing, musical guests, parking arrangements, and requested a one-day beer-and-wine license.

votes.motion: Nominate Amanda Moore for vice chair
Close the public hearing for St. Bonafice's special event license
Approve the special event license for Sounds of Jubilee (June 22, noon-8pm) and one-day beer/wine license for the same date and time
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Peter Schmidt as seasonal cemetery laborer
Ratify the appointment of Andrea Matson and Olivia Cornella as seasonal lifeguards
Approve the letter of support for Senate Bill 400 (Chapter 70 commission), as amended
Delegate the select board's noncriminal disposition enforcement authority for chapter 232 (unregistered vehicles) to the building commissioner
Declare items listed in the Council on Aging director's May 6, 2025 email (chairs, a bench, a piano) as surplus property

budget_items.topic: Clean Water State Revolving Fund storm water grant
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager announced a state storm water asset-management grant with a required local match, continuing prior storm water inventory work under the MS4 permit.
The town manager reported the year's Cultural Council award and said she would meet with the council chair to help advertise the funds to local applicants.

budget_items.topic: TC Pacios roof repair funding to be moved by warrant article
budget_items.what_was_said: Previously approved fall special town meeting funding for TC Pacios roof repair was specific to the portion of the building being decommissioned; the town manager said a future warrant article will be brought to move those funds to the portion of the building that remains.

budget_items.topic: Friends of the Library membership and annual library support
budget_items.what_was_said: An announcement noted the annual membership fee to join the Friends of the Library and that proceeds from the group's sale support the library's collection each year.

budget_items.topic: Select board budget vacancy funds for contractual minute-taking
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager noted there is a small amount of money and time in the select board's own budget, due to a staff vacancy, that could pay a 1099 contractor by the set of minutes to help catch up on board minutes through June 30.

budget_items.topic: Appraisal cost for 56 Cara Sell tax-title property
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said the appraisal of the tax-title property, needed before the board can decide whether to sell or hold it, was expected to cost more than originally quoted.
A board member noted, while discussing the Chapter 70 letter of support, that the local contribution cap under the state formula is unusually high and should be lowered.

decisions.decision: Extend the deadline for board and committee members to reapply or new applicants to apply from May 15 to May 30, for one more recruitment push targeted at boards with no applicants (e.g. the Conservation Commission).

Select board members reassigned themselves as liaisons to various boards and committees (e.g. Capital Planning and Council on Aging to the chair; Economic Development to Amanda Moore; Finance Committee, Library Trustees, Board of Assessors and Open Space to Renee Mi; Planning Board to Glenn Mloud; School Committee to Brian; Storm Water Task Force to Renee Mi; Municipal Building Design Committee to Brian).
Board agreed to organize a joint site visit, as a posted meeting, to the 56 Cara Sell tax-title property.
Board scheduled a joint select board/town manager goals-setting workshop for Monday, June 9 at 6 p.m. and agreed to cancel the regular June 10 meeting.

what_happened.line: The board voted to send a letter of support for state Senate Bill 400, which would create a commission to review the Chapter 70 school funding formula.
The board reorganized after the town election, electing a new chair, vice chair and clerk and seating two newly elected members.
Members reassigned themselves as liaisons to town boards and committees, including the School Committee, Finance Committee and Planning Board, for the new term.
The board discussed a townwide sick leave bank policy at length, including eligibility and enrollment rules, without finalizing it.
The board deferred a decision on the tax-title property at 56 Cara Sell pending an appraisal and agreed to hold a posted joint site visit.

why_it_matters: Chapter 70 sets a large share of state aid to the school budget, so a push to review its formula could affect future school funding here even though nothing changes immediately.
The liaison assignments determine which select board member is the point of contact for bodies residents may need to reach, including the School Committee and Finance Committee.
A townwide sick leave bank and the disposition of the 56 Cara Sell property both involve town costs and town-owned property that residents may see come back for a vote or public discussion.
watch_next: Sick leave bank policy expected back before the board in June
